figAW_tbl1: A five-row comparison table contrasting the collocation (pseudospectral) and pure Galerkin spectral approaches across the key design dimensions that distinguish them: collocation enforces the residual pointwise at discrete nodes, evaluates nonlinear terms by pointwise multiplication in physical space, yields dense non-symmetric differentiation matrices, imposes boundary conditions explicitly through matrix surgery, and rests on discrete quadrature bounds for stability; the Galerkin method instead enforces global orthogonality through an integral inner product, handles nonlinearities via convolution of coefficients, produces often symmetric, sparse, or banded matrices, satisfies boundary conditions implicitly through the design of the basis functions, and gains stability guarantees from continuous coercivity and energy norms. The takeaway is that collocation buys implementation simplicity and easy treatment of nonlinearities at the cost of dense, ill-conditioned operators, whereas Galerkin trades pointwise convenience for sparse, well-structured operators and rigorous stability.
